candidates: Within a function that normalizes a string parameter at the top (e.g., `str = str.trim()`), do not call the same normalization method on that variable again in subsequent expressions within the same function body; the variable is already in its normalized form.

New gantt diagram features must have test coverage at all three layers: DB-layer unit tests (`ganttDb.spec.ts`), parser-level unit tests (`packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/gantt/parser/gantt.spec.js`), and end-to-end rendering/visual snapshot tests (`cypress/integration/rendering/gantt.spec.js`). Tests that only exercise internal DB functions in isolation are insufficient on their own.

Use descriptive, semantically meaningful variable names instead of single-letter or terse abbreviations; for example, prefer `today` or `midnightDate` over `dt`, and `latestEndingTask` over abbreviated alternatives.

Structure conditional branches to avoid double negation by using positive conditions; put the positive/happy-path early return first and the fallback last — e.g., `if (task) { return task.value; } return fallback;` — rather than `if (!task) { return fallback; } else { return task.value; }`.

When extracting substrings from regular expression matches, use named capture groups (`(?<name>pattern)`) and reference them via `.groups.name` rather than positional numeric indices (e.g., `match[1]`). This applies throughout `ganttDb.js` and any other file that uses regex to parse diagram syntax.

When adding tests for new functionality in an existing test file, add new standalone test cases rather than modifying the content of existing ones. Existing test cases may intentionally exercise specific edge cases — such as inconsistent whitespace, unusual formatting, or deliberately invalid input — and altering or removing them silently drops that coverage.
